children: Brazil's Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Tuesday that Brazilian households spend about 60 billion reais ($11.6 billion) a year on online betting, while roughly 10 billion reais is collected by the government through taxes imposed by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's administration.

Speaking as a representative of Lula's economic platform ahead of the October election, Durigan said the leftist president "has shown himself to be strongly opposed to online betting" and that his administration would do whatever it can to further curb the sector in Brazil.
"We need to find even tougher ways to tackle it because it is a real problem," he said, without detailing possible actions, during a forum hosted by media outlets owned by Grupo Globo.
